fullPassage:
The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS (Global Positioning System) on our cell phones, no one can find their way about without it. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens full of pictures, rather than print media, such as books. It is thus possible that extensions of human faculties, through techno- and bio-enhancement, will bring about ____________________.

* techno-utopian: 기술 낙관론자 ** amputation: 절라내기, 절단 *** post-literate: 탈문해화의

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of (A)[dehumanization / humanization], and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who (B)[cautioned / encouraged] decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an (C)[amputation / augmentation].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 기술의 과잉 확장에 대한 가장 강한 비판은 비인간화(dehumanization)를 수반하며, McLuhan은 수십 년 전에 경고했다(cautioned). 그는 모든 미디어 확장이 절단(amputation)이라고 주장했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① dehumanization — cautioned — amputation: 원문 그대로
❌ ② humanization(인간화)은 반의어
❌ ③ encouraged(격려하다)는 cautioned(경고하다)의 반의어
❌ ④ augmentation(증대)은 amputation(절단)의 반의어
det.tip: dehumanization(비인간화) ↔ humanization / cautioned(경고) ↔ encouraged / amputation(절단) ↔ augmentation(증대)

questions.passage: Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming (A)[post-literate / pre-literate] because we rely on screens full of pictures, rather than print media, such as books. It is thus possible that extensions of human faculties, through techno- and (B)[bio-enhancement / bio-reduction], will bring about arrested development in the natural (C)[evolution / extinction] of higher human faculties.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: McLuhan의 철학에 따르면 우리는 탈문해화(post-literate)되고 있으며, 생체 향상(bio-enhancement)을 통한 인간 능력의 확장이 고등 인간 능력의 자연적 진화(evolution)의 정지를 초래한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② post-literate — bio-enhancement — evolution: 원문 일치
❌ ① pre-literate(문자 이전의)는 post-literate(탈문해화의)와 반대
❌ ③ bio-reduction(생체 축소)은 bio-enhancement(생체 향상)의 반의어
❌ ④ extinction(멸종)은 evolution(진화)과 다른 개념
det.tip: post-literate = 탈문해화(문자 너머 → 영상 의존). pre-literate = 문자 이전 시대

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the (A)[overextension / underuse] of technology involve claims of dehumanization. McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker. For example, once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS on our cell phones, no one can find their way about without it. We are becoming post-literate because we (B)[rely on / dismiss] screens full of pictures. It is thus possible that extensions of human faculties will bring about arrested development in the natural evolution of (C)[higher / lower] human faculties.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 기술의 과잉 확장(overextension)에 대한 비판 → 화면에 의존(rely on) → 고등(higher) 인간 능력의 진화 정지
det.analysis:
✅ ③ overextension — rely on — higher: 원문 일치
❌ ① underuse(과소 사용)는 overextension(과잉 확장)의 반의어
❌ ② dismiss(무시)는 rely on(의존)의 반의어
❌ ④ lower(하등)는 higher(고등)의 반의어
det.tip: overextension = 과잉 확장 ↔ underuse(과소 사용). rely on ↔ dismiss(무시하다)

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a ①<u>critical</u> thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously ②<u>claimed</u> that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to ③<u>remember</u> things. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens full of pictures, rather than ④<u>digital</u> media, such as books.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문에서 '책과 같은 인쇄(print) 매체'라고 했는데, ④에서 digital(디지털)로 바뀌어 있다. 화면에 의존한다는 맥락에서 대비되는 것은 인쇄 매체.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ digital → print: 원문은 'print media, such as books'. 화면(screens) vs 인쇄(print)의 대비
❌ ① critical(비판적) — 원문 그대로
❌ ② claimed(주장했다) — 원문 그대로
❌ ③ remember(기억하다) — 원문 그대로
det.tip: print media(인쇄 매체) ↔ digital media(디지털 매체). 책은 인쇄 매체!

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization. McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human ①<u>extension</u> into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS on our cell phones, no one can find their way about ②<u>with</u> it. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens full of ③<u>pictures</u>, rather than print media, such as books. It is thus possible that extensions of human faculties will bring about arrested ④<u>development</u> in the natural evolution of higher human faculties.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문에서 GPS가 있으니 '그것 없이는(without) 길을 찾지 못한다'인데, ②에서 with(~와 함께)로 바뀌어 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② with → without: 원문은 'no one can find their way about without it'. GPS 의존의 부정적 맥락
❌ ① extension(확장) — 원문 그대로
❌ ③ pictures(그림) — 원문 그대로
❌ ④ development(발달) — 원문 그대로
det.tip: without = ~없이 ↔ with = ~와 함께. 'no one can find their way without it' = GPS 없이는 아무도 길을 못 찾는다

questions.passage: The strongest ①<u>criticisms</u> of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an ②<u>expansion</u>. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens full of pictures, ③<u>rather than</u> print media, such as books. It is thus possible that extensions of human ④<u>faculties</u> will bring about arrested development.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문에서 McLuhan은 모든 미디어 확장이 절단(amputation)이라고 했는데, ②에서 expansion(확장)으로 바뀌어 있다. '확장은 곧 절단'이라는 역설이 핵심.
det.analysis:
✅ ② expansion → amputation: McLuhan의 핵심 주장. expansion(확장)은 긍정적이라 맥락에 맞지 않음
❌ ① criticisms(비판) — 원문 그대로
❌ ③ rather than(~보다는) — 원문 그대로
❌ ④ faculties(능력) — 원문 그대로
det.tip: amputation(절단) ↔ expansion(확장). McLuhan: 'every media extension = amputation'

questions.passage: The strongest __________ of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 기술의 과잉 확장에 대한 가장 강한 비판(criticisms)은 비인간화를 수반한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ criticisms(비판): 뒤에 dehumanization(비인간화) + cautioned(경고)라는 부정적 맥락
❌ ① extensions(확장) — 비판의 대상이지 비판 자체가 아님
❌ ② innovations(혁신) — 긍정적 뉘앙스
❌ ④ achievements(성취) — 긍정적 뉘앙스
det.tip: criticism(비판) — 'claims of dehumanization'이 이어지므로 부정적 맥락의 단어가 필요

questions.passage: Canadian philosopher Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS on our cell phones, no one can find their way about without it. Based on McLuhan's __________, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens full of pictures.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: McLuhan의 철학(philosophy)에 근거하여 우리는 탈문해화되고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① philosophy(철학): McLuhan의 사상/관점에 기반한 결론이라는 맥락
❌ ② biography(전기) — McLuhan의 생애가 아니라 그의 사상이 근거
❌ ③ technology(기술) — 비판 대상이지 근거가 아님
❌ ④ geography(지리학) — 맥락과 무관
det.tip: philosophy = 철학, 사상. 'Based on ~'s philosophy' = ~의 철학에 따르면

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization. McLuhan claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens full of pictures. It is thus possible that extensions of human __________, through techno- and bio-enhancement, will bring about arrested development.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 기술 및 생체 향상을 통한 인간 능력(faculties)의 확장이 발달 정지를 초래한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ faculties(능력): 걷기, 기억, 길찾기 등 구체적 인간 능력이 기술에 의해 대체된다는 맥락
❌ ① devices(장치) — 'human devices'는 부자연스러움
❌ ② networks(네트워크) — 인간 네트워크와 다른 맥락
❌ ③ ambitions(야망) — 야망의 확장이 arrested development를 초래한다는 것은 비논리적
det.tip: faculty = (신체/정신의) 능력, 기능. 복수형 faculties = 다양한 인간 능력

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who <u>cautioned</u> decades ago against too much human extension into technology.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 cautioned과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: cautioned = 경고하다. 'against too much ~'이라는 부정적 맥락에서 경고의 의미.
det.analysis:
✅ ② warned(경고하다): cautioned과 동의어
❌ ① praised(칭찬하다) — 반대 뉘앙스
❌ ③ promoted(장려하다) — 반대 뉘앙스
❌ ④ inspired(영감을 주다) — 다른 의미
det.tip: caution = warn = alert ↔ praise, promote, encourage

questions.passage: McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we <u>rely on</u> screens full of pictures, rather than print media, such as books.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 rely on과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: rely on = ~에 의존하다. 화면에 의존하여 인쇄 매체 대신 사용한다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ depend on(~에 의존하다): rely on과 동의어
❌ ① give up(포기하다) — 의미 다름
❌ ② look into(조사하다) — 의미 다름
❌ ④ break away from(~에서 벗어나다) — 반대 의미
det.tip: rely on = depend on = count on = lean on (의존하다 동의어군)

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology <u>involve</u> claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 involve과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: involve = 포함하다, 수반하다. 기술 비판이 비인간화 주장을 수반한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① include(포함하다): involve와 동의어
❌ ② exclude(배제하다) — involve의 반의어
❌ ③ resolve(해결하다) — 발음 유사하지만 의미 다름
❌ ④ evolve(진화하다) — 발음 유사하지만 의미 다름
det.tip: involve = include = entail. resolve, evolve와 어미(-olve) 혼동 주의

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the <u>overextension</u> of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. McLuhan claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 overextension과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: overextension = 과잉 확장 ↔ restriction = 제한, 억제
det.analysis:
✅ ② restriction(제한): overextension(과잉 확장)의 반의어
❌ ① expansion(확장) — overextension과 유사한 뉘앙스
❌ ③ domination(지배) — 관련 없음
❌ ④ penetration(침투) — 관련 없음
det.tip: overextension(과잉 확장) ↔ restriction(제한). expansion은 동의어에 가까우므로 반의어 아님

questions.passage: McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a <u>critical</u> thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 critical과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: critical = 비판적인 ↔ uncritical = 무비판적인
det.analysis:
✅ ④ uncritical(무비판적인): critical의 직접적 반의어
❌ ① analytical(분석적인) — critical과 유사
❌ ② skeptical(회의적인) — critical과 유사
❌ ③ rational(합리적인) — critical과 유사
det.tip: critical ↔ uncritical. analytical, skeptical, rational은 모두 critical과 비슷 → 반의어 아님

questions.passage:
(A) McLuhan famously claimed that every media <u>extension</u> of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk any more.

(B) The company approved a six-month <u>extension</u> of the deadline for submitting the final report.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 extension이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 인간의 미디어 확장(extension) = 능력을 기술로 넓히는 것 (B) 마감일의 연장(extension) = 기한을 늘리는 것
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 확장 — (B) 연장
❌ ① 의미가 뒤바뀜
❌ ② (A) 내선번호는 맥락과 무관
❌ ④ (B) 내선번호는 맥락과 무관
det.tip: extension 다의어: ① 확장(범위) ② 연장(기간) ③ 내선(전화번호)

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어는?

"the process of removing the human qualities from something, especially in a way that makes people feel less important"

det.korean: '무언가에서 인간적 특성을 제거하는 과정' = dehumanization(비인간화)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ dehumanization(비인간화): 인간적 특성 제거
❌ ① overextension(과잉 확장)
❌ ② amputation(절단)
❌ ③ enhancement(향상)
det.tip: de- + human + -ization = 인간(human)에서 벗어나게 만드는 것. de- 접두사 = 제거/반대

questions.passage: McLuhan __________ (famous) claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. This was one of his most well-known arguments.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: McLuhan은 유명하게(famously) 주장했다 — 동사 claimed를 수식하는 부사 형태
det.analysis: ✅ famously: famous(형용사) → famously(부사). 동사 claimed를 수식
det.tip: 형용사 → 부사: famous → famously, primary → primarily

questions.passage: McLuhan was a critical thinker. The __________ (strong) criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 기술 과잉 확장에 대한 가장 강한(strongest) 비판 — the + 최상급
det.analysis: ✅ strongest: 'the __________ criticisms'에서 the + 최상급. strong → strongest
det.tip: the + 최상급: the strongest, the biggest. stronger(비교급)는 'the + 비교급 of the two'에서만

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization. McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we __________; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: don't walk to the shops any more

det.korean: 차가 생기면 더 이상 가게에 걸어가지 않는다 — 기술이 인간 능력을 대체하는 예시
det.analysis:
✅ ② don't walk to the shops any more: 원문 그대로. 차 → 걷기 능력 상실
❌ ① drive faster — 속도 증가는 amputation 맥락과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ travel to distant countries — 본문 맥락과 다름
❌ ④ exercise more regularly — 본문과 무관
det.tip: amputation 예시 3가지: 차→걷기 상실, 하드드라이브→기억력 상실, GPS→길찾기 상실

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. McLuhan claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens full of pictures, rather than print media, such as books. It is thus possible that extensions of human faculties, through techno- and bio-enhancement, will bring about __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: arrested development in the natural evolution of higher human faculties
a return to traditional literacy through digital innovation

det.korean: 인간 능력의 확장이 고등 인간 능력의 자연적 진화의 정지(arrested development)를 초래한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ arrested development in the natural evolution of higher human faculties: 글 전체 논지의 결론
❌ ① rapid advancement — 발전이 아닌 정지가 논지
❌ ② greater freedom — 자유가 아닌 능력 상실이 논지
❌ ④ return to literacy — 탈문해화를 말하지 복귀를 말하지 않음
det.tip: arrested development = 발달 정지. arrest = 멈추게 하다
